title: PrefixSmith: automated prefix-key recommendations, hit-model, and staged TTL rollouts
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation:
We need an automated, low-risk system to recommend KV/prefix cache key designs and TTL policies that reduce per-token cost while keeping latency and error rates within SLOs. Current manual tuning ties up platform engineers and results in uneven outcomes across customers. PrefixSmith will ingest prefix usage telemetry, build a hit-rate model per-prefix, generate TTL and key-composition recommendations, and provide an orchestrated staged apply/rollback plan with safety gates.

Scope (what this ticket covers):
- Offline hit-rate model prototype using 30 days of prefix telemetry and sampled request traces.
- A recommendation engine that outputs: suggested TTL, suggested key normalization (e.g., affix trimming, canonicalization rules), and estimated cost delta and hit-rate uplift per prefix.
- Simulation harness to run a dry-run applying recommendations on historical traffic and produce regressionsafe forecasts.
- Staged rollout orchestration: dry-run -> shadow -> 1% canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic abort criteria and rollback.
- Dashboards and alerting for key KPIs.

Out of scope: automatic quantization or batching knobs (handled by separate workstream). On-prem install of rollout engine will be separate private deployment ticket.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Achieve >=10% per-token cost reduction on targeted backend pools in pilot accounts without increasing p95 latency by >5% and without customer-visible errors.
- Recommendations have an observed hit-rate uplift within +/-3% of model predictions in canary windows.
- Rollouts support automated abort/rollback rules and have run once in production dry-run with no incidents.

Monitoring & metrics to track:
- prefix_hit_rate (per prefix, 1m and 5m windows)
- induced_request_rate_change (percent requests altered by new keying)
- p50/p95/p99 latency for inference path
- errors_by_prefix and error_rate_total
- cost_per_1k_tokens_by_pool and delta from baseline
- rollout_safety_signals: CPU_spike, GPU_mem_pressure, increased_error_rate, missing_cache_kv

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Data collection & schema (Week 0-1): extract 30d telemetry: prefix, request_count, cache_hits, cache_misses, token_count, latency_histogram. Build an export job to S3 and a lightweight Parquet layout used by notebook simulations. Owner: Liam Chen.
2) Hit-rate model (Week 1-2): prototype a per-prefix estimator that predicts steady-state hit-rate as a function of TTL and prefix-aggregation rules. Use time-decayed popularity and simple Poisson arrival assumptions for baseline; implement a sampling-based bootstrap to produce confidence intervals. Deliverable: Jupyter notebook + model explainability export. Owner: Priya Nair.
3) Recommendation engine (Week 2-3): implement rules that convert model outputs to actionable suggestions: TTL value, normalization rules (strip session ids, map numeric suffixes to buckets), and a per-prefix confidence score. Output schema: prefix, suggestion_type, suggested_ttl_seconds, suggested_key_transform, estimated_hit_rate_gain_pct, estimated_cost_delta_usd_per_1M_tokens. Owner: Liam Chen.
4) Simulation & dry-run harness (Week 3): apply suggestions to historical logs and compute simulated downstream metrics and rollback risk. Owner: Marco Diaz.
5) Rollout orchestration & safety gates (Week 3-4): new rollout controller supports phased apply and automatic rollback on gate violations. Define gates (latency p95 +5%, error_rate +0.5ppt, cost_spike >10%). Owner: SRE (Ashwin Rao).
6) Dashboards & alerts (Week 4): Grafana panels and alert rules for all KPIs. Owner: Observability team (Elena Park).
7) Pilot (Week 5): run on two internal pilot accounts and validate metrics. Iterate.

Acceptance criteria (explicit):
- [ ] Notebook with model and low-level simulation reproduces historical hit-rates within 5% on a holdout period.
- [ ] Recommendation engine produces suggestions for >=80% of top-1k prefixes by traffic.
- [ ] Rollout controller executes staged apply and triggers rollback in a simulated error injection test.
- [ ] Grafana dashboard and alerts created; on-call runbook updated with abort steps.
- [ ] Pilot run completed on two accounts and postmortem with lessons learned published.
acceptance_criteria: Notebook reproduces historical hit-rates within 5% on holdout

risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Misapplied key normalization may group distinct signals and cause quality regressions. Mitigation: conservative confidence thresholds, manual approval for top-100 revenue prefixes.
Risk: Rollout aborts could oscillate and cause flapping. Mitigation: minimum stable window and exponential backoff for retries after rollback.
Risk: Underestimated cold-start effect when increasing TTL. Mitigation: simulate cold-start scenarios and apply warmup policies for low-traffic prefixes.
postmortem_plan: If pilot causes customer-visible impact, run incident review within 72 hours, collect telemetry snapshots for the rollout window, and update normalization rules and decision thresholds. Publish postmortem to Confluence and share with GTM and support.
notes: This ticket is intentionally conservative: recommendation confidence must reach 'high' before auto applying to >10% traffic. Lower-confidence suggestions are surfaced as operator recommendations behind a 'suggestions' UI.
